sections.title: Marketing on Facebook Marketplace
sections.blurb: Your own listings from your own profile, never the same ad twice, the auto-reply, the inbox and your Claude.
sections.body_md:
**Sales** > **Marketing**. You post CarmaCars cars on Facebook Marketplace from your own Facebook profile, answer the Marketplace inbox, and log what you did. The numbers you collect are leads credited to you.

## Never the same ad twice

Each car can have up to 5 live listings across the team (the owner's own listing included). Every listing is a different **copy variant**: its own title, its own description wording, its own photo order and its own cover photo. When you claim a car, its variant is yours until you take the listing down or it lapses: no one else can post that copy. You can have one listing of a car at a time.

- A claim you do not post within a day lets go by itself.
- A listing ends 30 days after you posted or renewed it, unless you renew it.
- The Admin sees who posted what, with the listing's address.

## Today

1. **Today** lists your work in this order: **Take down**, **Update the price**, **Post it** (a car you claimed), then **Renew** and new **Post** items, up to your posts and renewals for the day (4 by default).
2. On a **Post** item press **Claim variant** with its number. Then press **Kit**.
3. The kit shows every field of facebook.com/marketplace/create/vehicle in order, each with **Copy**, your variant's description and tracked link, and the photos in your order. Press **Download the photos (ZIP)**: 01 is your cover. **With scenes (ZIP)** takes the car's marketing set instead (its photos in other scenes, made on its listing).
4. Post it on Facebook, open the new listing and copy its address. Back on **Today**, press **Posted** and paste the address. **Let go** frees a claim you will not post.
5. Press **Renewed**, **Updated** or **Taken down** when you do those on Facebook.

## Words to use

Nothing a buyer reads says "rent", "rental" or "for rent". Every listing keeps the line "Daily and weekly bookings only, not for sale" and the price is for one day. The kit and the replies already follow this.

## The auto-reply

**Auto-reply for this listing** has the steps and the text, with your listing's own link. While posting, scroll to **Auto replies** (or **Meta AI replies**), turn it on, replace the draft with the text, then publish. It only answers the first "Is this available?".

## The inbox

1. Open facebook.com/marketplace/inbox, the Selling tab, oldest first.
2. Use **Inbox replies for this car** only: price, availability, requirements, deposit, delivery, send your number. One message per reply, at most two to someone who does not answer.
3. Then **Log an inbox session**: the chats, the replies and every number, one per line (name, phone, car code). Each new number is a lead credited to you, with a call-back task within 15 minutes.

## Your own Claude

**Your Claude in Chrome** has the instructions to paste into Claude in your own Chrome, and the **Academy lesson** that teaches them. Claude follows the same rules: the kit's words and the templates only, it stops at any Facebook security check or CAPTCHA and tells you, it never types a password, and it logs every post in your Marketing tab.

> Watch out: Stop and tell the Admin if Facebook removes a listing or restricts your account. Do not appeal and do not post it again.

## Event pages

Below Marketplace, **Event pages** lists the Toronto and GTA events with a "Rent a car for" page. Press **Add an event** for a new one, or **Edit** to set its dates once the organiser announces them, with the organiser's page as the source. Share an event page in your posts in the weeks before it.

## Email campaigns

**Marketing** > **Email campaigns** shows the marketing audience (everyone who gave us their email on the site, minus anyone who unsubscribed), the weekly email and the email for each new car: waiting, queued, sent and unsubscribed. Read only: the Admin changes the switches.

sections.title: Add a rental by hand
sections.blurb: Choose the car and dates, find the renter, price it, record how it is paid.
sections.body_md:
Every function adds rentals that come in by phone, at the counter, from Turo, a partner, an insurer or someone you know. The rental is confirmed and on the calendar at once.

## Add a rental

Open **Bookings**, the **Add a rental** button. Your home address must be in your profile first: until it is, the page asks for it.

1. At pickup with the renter? Press **Start at pickup**: the renter's name and phone, the car, the kilometres and the fuel, then **Hold the car and finish later**. The car is held for 2 hours and you get a task to finish it.
2. Nothing is required to save: the form is saved as a draft as you type (**Save draft** saves at once). Unfinished rentals, on Today and on this page, opens a draft where it was left, on any device. Tick Hold the car while I finish to keep the car off the calendar while you type.
3. Choose the car, the dates and the places. The check shows any clash with another booking or with the cleaning time after a trip. You cannot book over a clash: ask an Admin.
4. The dates decide the case, shown under them. Car already out with the renter? Enter the pickup as when it left: the rental is recorded as on trip, and anything still missing (signature, licence check, coverage proof, deposit) becomes a task. A rental that has already ended is recorded by an Admin.
5. Find the renter by name, email or phone, or add a new one with their name, email, phone, date of birth and licence. A renter on file shows their licence, home address and the drivers named before (**Add them** puts those drivers on the rental), with an expired licence or an old address flagged. Add any other drivers.
6. The calendar and the price are checked by themselves once the car and the dates are in. The price comes from the rate sheet. You may add the extras, how damage is covered and an allowed promo code.
7. Quick start: **Phone**, **Walk-in**, **Turo or another platform** or **Insurance replacement** sets the usual choices.
8. A car tagged Listing not finished can be rented too: it stays off the public site. If it has no rates yet, type the rental charge for the whole rental and the reason. An owner's car not yet on the fleet insurance policy is added by an Admin only.
9. Every line of the price can be changed where it stands (customer service and sales, while Program settings allow it): the rental charge for the trip or a rate a day, the young driver fee, the Protection Plan, delivery, each add-on, the kilometres a day; add a fee from the list or a charge of its own. The (i) beside each line says what it is. The rate-sheet price stays on the booking; a price far under it is flagged for an Admin, never refused. Know what the renter paid with tax? Choose After tax (HST included) under Amounts I type and type those amounts ("$270 after tax for the rental, $50 for the Protection Plan"), or type the Total the renter pays (after tax): the rental charge is worked out so the total is exactly that. The total shown is the total saved.
10. Any length: past 30 days the monthly rate applies for each 30 days, and the monthly periods are listed. Each later period gets its own agreement, sent to the renter to sign a few days before it starts (Monthly periods on the booking; Send the agreement for the next period now if needed).
11. Choose how the rent is paid (e-Transfer or cash received, card on file, payment link, platform payout, insurer billed later; the ways open to you are set by an Admin; paid in parts: Add another payment) and then how the deposit is paid (card hold, cash or e-Transfer with its reference). Before you save sums it all up. The rental agreement is sent to the renter to sign online (never on paper). An insurance replacement with dates not known yet: untick Blocks the car's calendar and say why. Insurer billed later shows Charges to the insurer: type the rate a day of VLF, LDW, T&LDW, PAP/PEC or Waiver Saver that the insurer authorized (empty: none); each is the rate times the days, plus HST, billed to the insurer.
12. Under Who found this client, choose **I sourced this client** or **Entered for CarmaCars**.
13. Press **Add the rental**. The renter gets the confirmation email unless you tick **Do not email the renter**.
14. A rental you add is credited to you and shows in My sales as a rental you added. If you sourced it, its commission shows there too.

> Tip: The renter signs the rental agreement in their portal before pickup. With the saved card, nothing is charged when you add the rental: the card is charged when the renter presses Accept and sign. At the counter, they sign on the phone with **Sign now on this device**. A payment link keeps the booking waiting for payment.

sections.title: Commissions
sections.blurb: I sourced this client, your rate, when it is earned, approved and paid.
sections.body_md:
Sales (and field staff) earn a commission on the rentals they source: a renter you found yourself. Say so when you enter the rental, the quote or the offer. Customer service, Fleet and Finance earn no commission and no sales credit: your help is credited on the booking (Helped by) and on your scorecard.

## Mark who found the client

Every rental, quote and offer you enter asks: **I sourced this client** or **Entered for CarmaCars**.

1. Choose **I sourced this client** when you found the renter yourself: someone you know, your own post or your own outreach.
2. Choose **Entered for CarmaCars** when the renter came to CarmaCars: the website, the phone line, a walk-in, a partner.
3. A website request earns nothing by itself. If you sourced it anyway, choose I sourced this client on its offer: an Admin decides.

|  | Commission |
| --- | --- |
| Sales | Commission only, with no base pay. By the rental days of the month, on all of that month's rentals: in person under 50 days 10%, from 50 days 15%, from 100 days 20%; remote 5%, 10% and 15%, one tier lower in a month under 400 touches (chapter Sales) |
| Customer service, Fleet, Finance | No commission and no sales credit, whichever you choose above. Your help is credited as Helped by on the booking and counted on your scorecard |
| An owner you bring in (Sales) | What you ask for and an Admin approves: a flat amount at the owner's first paid rental, or a percent of their cars' rentals for a time (chapter Sales). A CarmaCars expense: it never changes the owner's revenue |
| How much | The rate on the rental charge before tax, after discounts, with late extra days, plus the add-ons (release 35: the same rate on each confirmed add-on's own charge before tax; not prepaid fuel). Never on delivery, kilometres, young driver, the Protection Plan or other fees. Only a refund of the rental charge, or an add-on removed after booking, comes off |
| When earned | When the rental is completed and paid in full. Never on a cancelled, refunded, unpaid or charged-back rental, or on your own or a household rental |
| Your home address | It must be in your profile. Until it is, a commission waits as not earned yet, and you cannot add a rental or mark I sourced this client |
| Paid | After an Admin approves it, by transfer or on your pay statement. My sales shows each step: not earned yet, pending approval, approved, paid, reversed |

> Tip: A refund or chargeback after a commission was paid comes off your next payment. Your staff agreement has the full rule.

sections.title: Academy
sections.blurb: Your training path: lessons narrated by your browser, a quiz per section, 80% to pass.
sections.body_md:
Your training path is under **Me** > **Academy**. There is a path for each of your functions: customer service, fleet, finance, Sales in person or remote, field work.

## Watch the lessons

1. Open **Academy**. Each path lists its sections in order, with Passed, Open or Pass the one before.
2. Open a section. Each lesson is a short video made by your browser: scenes with captions, read aloud by your browser's own voice.
3. Press **Play**. **Pause**, **Back** and **Next** move through the scenes; **Replay** starts again; Speed goes from 0.75x to 1.5x. **Voice on** turns the voice off and on.
4. No sound or no English voice on your device? The lesson plays with captions only, each scene timed for reading.

> Tip: Use headphones in the office. The voice is your browser's, so it can sound different on another device.

## Pass the quiz

1. Under the lessons, answer every question and press **Check my answers**.
2. You need 80% (the pass mark in Program settings). Passed: the next section opens. Not yet: each answer shows the right one and why; press **Try again** as often as you need.
3. A section that is on two of your paths (the policies, for example) counts on both once passed.

> Good to know: An Admin can open a section early for you, for example when you already did this work somewhere else. The academy gate is on: each section opens once you pass the one before it. If you were hired with one-step Hire, the rest of the portal waits until you pass your paths (the guide and your profile stay open). Each path ends with a section on what changed recently.

## Your first steps: Welcome (release 34)

Your first sign-in opens **Welcome**, your onboarding checklist, in four steps:

1. Welcome.
2. Your profile and phone: add your home address and your mobile number in your profile.
3. The academy: pass every section of your path. Each quiz passes at 80%, and you can retake it as often as you need.
4. Your first tasks: press **Done** on each one as you finish it.

Until you pass the academy, Welcome, the academy, the guide and your profile are all that opens; any other page brings you back to Welcome. Then **Go to your portal** opens everything.

## Quiz rules (release 35)

A quiz passes at 90%. Questions come in a random order and open after the reading time. After a failed try, wait 30 minutes; you have 3 tries a day. New sections for your role are added to your path: if you had passed everything, you keep a week before they hold you, and nothing you passed is reset.

sections.title: Live visitors and live chat
sections.blurb: Who is on the site, how likely each visitor is to book, one-click actions, follow-ups, the chat inbox.
sections.body_md:
Customer service and Sales see who is on the site now and answer the live chat. The CarmaCars assistant answers first; you take over whenever you want.

## Live visitors

1. Open **Visitors**: the map on top with its clusters and cards (Show contact shows phones and emails), and **Live now** under it; **History** lists the visits before (customer service and Sales). "Live now" counts who is on the site now, "Visitors today" the people seen today. The page refreshes by itself every 15 seconds; the menu shows how many hot visitors are on the site. Each visitor shows a booking likelihood from 0 to 100 (Hot, Warm or Cold); the most likely to book come first.
2. "Why" gives the three strongest reasons, for example "Pickup tomorrow · Saw $320 for 3 days · Tapped to call". The badges are all the signals; the dots say how strong each is.
3. Each visitor shows a name when known, otherwise "Visitor from Toronto, phone", the page and car they are on, how many others look at that car now, and this visit's pages.
4. Suggested: the next step and a message. Press **Invite to chat with this message**, or **Edit the message** first. Sales can **Offer a 10% discount code** (one per visitor a week). **Assign to Sales** hands the visitor to Sales with a task. When their dates are taken, **Suggest a similar free car** writes the message for you.
5. Press **Pages** for the whole visit. Press **Start a chat** to write your own short friendly message and press **Send**: the visitor sees it in a bubble.
6. A hot visitor raises an alert at the top of the page. Each action shows on the visitor ("Invited by Lena, 2 min ago"), so check it before writing.

## Name a visitor

When you learn who a visitor is (they called, or told you in the chat), press **Name** on their line, type the name and, if you have them, their phone, email and a note, then press **Save the name**. The name shows on Live visitors, Visitor history and Live chat, and on every later visit from the same browser. Only staff see it. A phone you add also saves them as a contact in Quo. If they later book or sign in, the name the booking has replaces yours. **Edit name** changes it; **Remove the name** takes it off.

## Follow-ups

Signals of known visitors raise tasks on To do with what to do, for example "Call or message Maya Chen: opened offer CC-1042 twice, no answer for 6 hours". Call or message, then mark the task done. A task closes by itself when the renter answers or pays. Follow-ups done count in My sales.

Renters also get one polite reminder email (and at most one more) when they leave an offer, the pay page or a change unanswered. Taking the follow-up task, a chat with you or a message from you stops these reminders: you are handling it.

## Live chat

1. Open **Visitors** and press the **Chat** tab. The menu counts the chats that need a reply (waiting for a person, or the visitor wrote last). Reply within 5 minutes.
2. Choose a conversation. Beside it: the visitor's page, pages and signals, and the renter's bookings when known.
3. Press **Take over** (or just write a reply): the assistant stops. Write and press **Send** or Enter. The visitor sees when you type.
4. **Hand back to the assistant** when you are done, or **Close**. A visitor who gave an email gets a copy of the chat.
5. Each new visitor message that waits for staff sends one alert (the bell, and your phone with phone alerts on). Tick "Email me when a chat waits (while I am on shift)" or desktop alerts if you want them too.
6. A visitor who left the site for 10 minutes: with no phone or email the chat closes (**Visitor left, no contact**); with one it shows **Follow up by text/email** and the task is in your queue. Text or email them, then mark the task done. If they come back, the chat opens again.
7. **AI replies paused** at the top says why the assistant is not answering; a staff note in the chat says the same. Answer the visitor yourself.

> Tip: Prices: send a quote from New quote, never a price from memory. If you handled the chat, choose "I sourced this client" on the quote; nothing is credited by itself.

## Alerts on your phone

The bell at the top of the menu opens **Alerts**, the list of everything for you; the same alerts reach your phone once phone alerts are on (**Alerts** > **Settings**). You get:

- A new lead assigned to you, or, when nobody has it, any new lead while you are on duty (live chat, Live visitors or Texts open in the last 15 minutes): contact form, phone number box, discount game claim or live chat. The alert names the source.
- A request someone typed into the booking request or contact form and did not send.
- A new owner lead assigned to you, if you are in Sales, and the unfinished application that became a lead to chase.
- A visitor turning Hot on Live visitors, while you are on duty.
- Your function's alerts while on duty: customer service the licences to review, complaint words, agreements not signed 2 hours before pickup and insurance proof missing; Sales offers about to expire; Fleet cars going out and back, no-shows, cancellations, cards declined at pickup and the tracker alerts.
- An urgent alert a colleague did not open in 15 minutes ("Passed to you").
- A morning brief at 8 am of your own work.

1. Open the alert to land on its page. **Call** on the phone alert opens your dialer with the number; **Send offer**, **Approve** or **Decline** open the booking.
2. Call or text the person first; the task closes by itself when they send the form.
3. Too many? In **Alerts** > **Settings** turn a topic off, set your quiet hours (normal alerts wait until they end), or turn on focus mode (only urgent ones for 1 or 3 hours). Bursts arrive as one alert.
4. **Snooze 30 min** on an urgent alert brings it back in 30 minutes; it is not passed on meanwhile.

> Tip: urgent alerts come at any hour, whatever your quiet hours.

sections.title: Texts and calls
sections.blurb: Reading and answering texts, suggestions, unknown callers and missed calls.
sections.body_md:
Customer service and Sales answer texts to the CarmaCars number in the same place as live chat. Every call and text is kept with the renter, owner or lead it belongs to.

## Answer a text

1. Open **Visitors**, the **Chat** tab, and press **Texts and calls**. Unread texts and missed calls are counted on each number.
2. Choose a number: calls and texts in order, and beside them who it is, with their bookings.
3. Write the text and press **Send text**. It goes from the CarmaCars number.
4. **Suggest a reply** writes a draft into the box. Read it and change it: it is never sent until you press Send text.

## Unknown callers

Press **Unknown callers**. Type the name if they told you and press **Create lead**, or find the renter and press **Link to** their name.

Quo's contacts follow the site: everyone on the site with a phone number is a contact in Quo under the same name, added or updated within about five minutes. Change a name or number on the site, not in Quo: the site's version is sent again.

## Missed calls

A missed call gives you the task "Missed call from ..." when you have Live chat or Texts and calls open; otherwise it waits in the customer service queue. Call back with the Call button, or text, then mark the task done. Quo itself texts the caller back, so do not send the same message again.

> Tip: A number that texted STOP gets no texts from us, booking texts included, until they text START. Prices go in a quote, never in a text from memory.

## Email, text or both

Each renter and owner chooses how we reach them. Their page in Admin shows it under How we reach them; ask an Admin, or change it there if you can open the page. Texts need a phone they verified with a code. Your own choice is on your Profile, under Messages.


## Call and Text buttons

Every Call and Text button in the staff portal (a booking, a renter, the Now view, the map's cards, Visitors, the field jobs) goes through Quo, from the CarmaCars number.

1. Press **Text**: a small window opens with the person and the number. Write the text (sign it CarmaCars) and press **Send**. It goes out from the CarmaCars number at once and is kept in the person's conversation under **Visitors** > **Chat** > **Texts and calls** (customer service and Sales); press **Open the conversation** to see it there. A number that asked for no texts is refused with the reason.
2. Press **Call**: on a phone the Quo app opens with the number in its dialer; press call there. On a computer the Quo web app opens in a new tab and the number is copied: open the dialer (Alt+C, or Ctrl+C on a Mac) and paste it. If Quo's desktop app is your computer's calling app, tick **On this computer, call with the Quo desktop app** once: Call then opens it straight away. Every call is noted on the conversation as Call started from the site, and Quo adds the call itself when it ends.
3. Fleet, finance and field staff can call and text the people of their work (renters, owners, leads and staff); customer service and Sales any number.
4. An Admin can switch the buttons back to the phone's own apps in Program settings. With Phone and texts off, the buttons use the phone's own apps too.

## Who is calling: the caller pop-up (release 34)

Customer service: when someone calls the CarmaCars number, a panel opens at the bottom right of every page of your portal (across the bottom on a phone) while the phone rings, and stays while the call goes on and for 3 minutes after it ends.

1. A renter: their name, the booking on rent (or the next one coming) with the car, the balance they owe now (**overdue** when a payment is late), the deposit (held, waived, released, or not taken yet), what they are waiting on (a request, an offer, a change, a question to them, an open To do) and the last three notes.
2. Write what the call was about in **Note about this call** and press **Add note**. It is kept on the renter with the time, your name and the booking.
3. **Open the renter's page** opens their record. If it is outside your window, opening it from their call is logged as an opening for 24 hours with the reason Incoming call, as **Open with a reason** is.
4. An unknown number shows **Unknown caller**: press **Create lead** to keep it as a phone lead.
5. Press the line at the top right of the call to minimize it: it becomes a small chip at the bottom of the page with the caller's name and the call's timer. Clicking anywhere outside the panel, or pressing Esc, minimizes it too. Press the chip to open the call again.
6. Press the cross to close a call; it stays closed in this browser. A new call always opens by itself.

## The Call helper (release 43)

Inside every call on the pop-up, the **Call helper** tells you what to say and do. It is made for your first weeks; press **Hide** when you no longer need it (**Show** brings it back).

1. **Say**: the greeting to read out, with your first name, and the caller's name and booking when we know them. Start every call with it.
2. **What is the call about?** Press the button that fits: New booking or price question, Change or extend a booking, Running late or late return, Pick-up and delivery, Deposit and payments, Insurance and protection, Accident or damage, Complaint, Owner wants to list a car, or Job applicant. You get 3 to 6 short steps. Words in bold quotes are what to say; a link opens the right page of your portal. **All situations** goes back.
3. **Search the quick answers**: type a word (deposit, late, cancel, km) for the short answer to the questions callers ask most.
4. The amounts, days and percentages in the steps and answers come from the settings, so they are always the ones in force. Never quote a price from memory: the offer screen works it out.
5. Always finish with **Note about this call**.

> Good to know: An Admin writes the greetings, the steps and the answers. Something wrong or missing? Tell an Admin: they change it in Settings and you see it on the next call.

## Renter notes (release 34)

A renter's record (**Find a renter**, then Open) has **Add a note**, and the notes are in its Activity log (chip **Notes**), newest first, each with the date and time, who wrote it and their role. Add a note for every situation: what they asked, what you told them, what happens next. Notes cannot be changed or removed by staff, so write a new note to correct one; an Admin can remove a note with a reason. The notes also show on the caller pop-up and on a renter's conversation in Texts and calls.

## Lanes, the Call button and hidden numbers (release 35)
1. Each conversation has a lane: **Fleet** for a car on rent, or a pickup, return, delivery or collection within a day; **Customer service** for the rest. The inbox has a tab for each. The caller pop-up rings for Fleet first on Fleet's calls; customer service gets them when no Fleet staff member is on duty or nobody answered within 20 seconds.
2. **Call** places the call in your browser (release 44, below): the customer sees the CarmaCars number, and the call is noted on their history with its length. Until calling from the site is set up, **Call** opens Quo as before and says why.
3. Sales sees customer numbers hidden, like (647) •••-••00. Use **Call** and **Text** on the page: the number is found on our side. Search by phone still works.

## Calls in your browser (release 44)

You make and take calls in the staff portal, in your browser, on the CarmaCars number. Your own phone number is never used and never shown, wherever you work from.

1. Use a computer with a headset (or earphones with a microphone) in Chrome, Edge or Safari. The first time you call, the browser asks to use the microphone: press **Allow**.
2. Press **Call** on a lead, a renter, a booking or any staff page. A bar opens at the bottom left of the page (at the top on a phone): **Calling ...**, then the call's timer once they answer. The customer sees the CarmaCars number. Sales: the number stays hidden, the call goes through all the same.
3. During the call: **Mute**, **Keypad** (for a phone menu that asks you to press a number) and **Hang up**. Do not close or reload the page during a call: that ends it.
4. Incoming calls: when someone calls the CarmaCars number, your browser rings while a staff page is open (customer service and Sales by default). Press **Answer** or **Decline**. The first person to answer takes the call and the others stop ringing. You see the caller's name when we know it (Sales: the number hidden).
5. Nobody online, or nobody answers: the caller hears a short message, and it is a missed call with its task, like every missed call. A call is never forwarded to your own phone.
6. Keep a staff page open during your shift with the computer's sound on, so you hear the ring.
7. A call that fails (the microphone not allowed, the connection lost): the bar says what to do. Press **Close**, fix it and call again.

## Calls first, texts after (release 37)

Your main priority is always to be on the phone with people.

1. Answer a ringing call before anything else, and return a missed call at once.
2. **Call before you text.** On a lead, a renter or a booking, **Call** is the first button and **Text** the second.
3. A text is a follow-up: after a call attempt (no answer, a voicemail left), or when the person asked for a text.
4. On your To do and on **Unanswered**, missed calls and call-backs are listed above unanswered texts.

## A lead you handle on a call (release 37)

When you answer or place a call with a lead, add a note on it, or create it from a call, the lead is yours for a limited time (15 minutes, as a Sales claim; an Admin can change it in **Settings** > **Sales**). Every call you handle adds the time again.

- Sales see **Being handled by** your first name and your function with the time, on the lead and in every list. They cannot claim it, call, text or email it, or set an outcome meanwhile, and **Next lead** skips it.
- Another customer service or Fleet person can still work it; their call or note takes the hold over.
- When it ends, the lead goes back to the salesperson who had a claim on it or who brought it, else to the open list. An Admin can **Release hold** earlier.
- A booking made from the lead is credited as always: customer service and Fleet get no sales commission for it.
- Nobody who has not finished onboarding holds a lead.

## Calling from the site: your mobile (release 40)

**Call** on a lead, a renter, a request or a booking rings your own mobile first, then connects the person. They see the CarmaCars number, never yours. Sales see the number hidden and call this way only.

1. The first time, with no mobile on your profile, a small window asks **Your mobile number**. Type your Canadian or US mobile (10 digits, for example (647) 555-0123) and press **Save and call**. No code is texted: it is saved to your profile and the call starts.
2. Your phone rings. Answer it: you hear "CarmaCars call. Connecting you now." and the person's phone rings.
3. A call that cannot start says why in the same window, with **Try again**. Calling from the site not set up: ask customer service or an Admin to call, and tell an Admin.
4. To add your number as a sign-in, use **Profile** > **Sign-in** > **Add and verify my phone number**. No code after a minute? Press **Resend the code**, or **Save it without a code**: calls still ring it, but you sign in with your email until it is verified.

sections.title: Discount game leads
sections.blurb: Game leads to call or email, the code they won, whether it is used, and the Sales task.
sections.body_md:
Visitors who are not signed in play a quick game on the site and win a promo code. To get it they give a first name, an email and sometimes a mobile number. Customer service and Sales follow them up.

## Game leads

**More customer service** > **Renters**, the **Leads** tab (Sales: **More sales**).

1. Each claim: when, the name (and "on the site now"), email and phone, the prize, the code and whether it is used, marketing consent, and the cars and pages they viewed.
2. Press **Call** or **Email**. Help them pick a car and send a request; the code goes in the promo code box (on their own device it is filled in). Then press **Contacted**.
3. **Close** with a reason when there is nothing more to do. A booking with the code marks the lead converted by itself.

A visitor who viewed 3 cars or more also raises a Sales task, for example "Claimed 10% off, viewed 6 cars: Maya". It closes when the code goes on a request. A visitor who wins another go plays a second game first; only the code they end with shows here.

People can win again: a day after their last code the game comes back on their next visit, and a new code is a new line with "2nd code of 2" under the name. It is the same person: one call covers both codes, and while their Sales task is open the new code is added to it instead of a second task. Each code is for one booking and never combined with another; an earlier code they have not used stays good until it ends.

> Tip: Without marketing consent, talk only about their request and the code they asked for: no other offers. The code takes up to $75 off the rental charge (a percentage), or $50 off a rental of 3 days or more, on one booking within 7 days.

## Contact details typed into forms

The card "Typed into forms" above the game leads lists the name, email and phone people typed into a form on the site without sending it, with "On the site now" and "Email not confirmed". Call or email to help them finish. Only what they typed; no offers without their consent.

sections.title: Add-ons
sections.blurb: Add-ons in offers and rentals, confirming a chauffeur, Fleet tasks and stock.
sections.body_md:
Renters buy add-ons with a rental: seats, flowers, a chauffeur, an umbrella, a phone charger, a full tank. You add them in offers and rentals, confirm the ones that need it, and Fleet keeps the stock.

## In an offer or a rental you add

1. On the review screen of a request, under Add-ons, tick or count what the renter wants. The price on the right follows. Choose the hours for a chauffeur.
2. Add-ons the renter asked for are already ticked. One waiting for confirmation (a chauffeur) is confirmed when you keep it and send the offer; untick it to remove it.
3. In **Bookings**, the **Add a rental** button, the Add-ons list sits under The rental: tick them before you press **Check the calendar and the price**.
4. Notice is yours to judge: you may add flowers with less than 24 hours if Fleet can do it.

## After booking

1. The booking page shows the add-ons, paid or not, and any waiting for confirmation.
2. A renter asked for a chauffeur from their portal: you get a task. Press **Confirm and charge** (the card on file is charged) or **Decline**.
3. Press **Remove** and give the reason to take one off. Unpaid, it goes; paid, a refund for it waits for approval.

## Fleet: tasks and stock

Flowers and a chauffeur give Fleet a task to get them ready, due before pickup by their notice.

1. Open **Cars** > **Add-ons**. Each add-on shows its price, its notice and how many are booked in the next 30 days.
2. For seats, umbrellas and chargers, type how many we have under In stock and press **Save**. Renters cannot ask for more than are free for their dates.
3. A confirmed booking with more than we have gives you an urgent task: find another or tell the renter.

Since release 35 your commission counts the add-ons at your same rate (not prepaid fuel); an add-on removed after booking leaves it. Sales cannot remove a paid add-on: ask customer service.

An add-on not returned has a charge in the agreement's fine print (Program settings); the deposit review shows it as a suggestion for Fleet and Finance.

sections.title: Assistant
sections.blurb: Ask about today, bookings, cars and money; send offers and add rentals; confirm the changes it prepares.
sections.body_md:
The assistant answers questions from live data and prepares changes for you. It works only through the same steps as the screens, with your own permissions: it cannot see or do anything you could not do yourself. Nothing changes until you confirm.

## Open it

Press **Assistant** at the top of the menu, or press Ctrl and / together (Cmd and / on a Mac). Esc closes it.

1. Type a question or what you want done, in your own words, and press Enter. Examples: "What needs doing today?", "Who has the Tesla?", "Is the Corolla free from 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-04?", "Find booking R-000123".
2. Answers come as cards with links: open one to go straight to the screen.
3. If something is missing or more than one thing matches, it asks and lists the choices. Press the one you mean.

## Changes: a card to confirm

1. Ask for a change, for example "Record a $900 e-Transfer on INV-1053 dated 2026-10-15 reference CA12345".
2. The assistant shows a card: "Record a $900 e-Transfer on INV-1053 for Jordan Price, dated Oct 15?". Read it, then press **Confirm** or **Cancel**.
3. Confirmed, it runs the same step as the screen and its pop-up, with the same checks. If the step is not allowed for you, or a detail is wrong, it says why and nothing changes.
4. Every change is in the audit log under your name, marked "via assistant". A card older than 30 minutes no longer runs: ask again.

Messages: ask it to draft a message to a renter or an owner. It writes the text; press **Copy**, open the conversation and send it yourself.

## Offers, rentals and what is owed (customer service and sales)

1. Send an offer: "Send an offer for the Corolla to jane@example.com, Nov 2 10:00 to Nov 4 10:00". A customer on file is found by name, email or phone; a new customer needs the full name, email, mobile and date of birth. Say "I found this client" when you did, so the booking counts for you.
2. The card shows the customer, the car, the dates, each price line, the HST, what is due at booking, the deposit, how it is paid and how the offer is sent, priced as **Send an offer** prices it. Press **Confirm** to make and send it, or **Cancel**.
3. Add a rental the same way: "Add a rental of the Corolla for jane@example.com, Nov 2 10:00 to Nov 4 10:00, paid by e-Transfer ref CA123, deposit in cash". Amounts after tax are understood: "$270 after tax for the rental and $50 after tax for the Protection Plan", or "$320 total after tax".
4. What is owed: "What does booking R-000123 owe?" shows the rental, fees and later charges still open, and the deposit. Finance sees it too.
5. Only what your function may do from the screens is offered; the booking's history says it was made with the staff assistant, with your name.

> Tip: The assistant keeps 70% of the day's free AI allowance for itself, so it works all day. When the whole allowance is used, it says how much was used and that it is back at midnight, Toronto time. Everything still works from the screens and pop-ups.

sections.title: Car maintenance
sections.blurb: The maintenance list, recording a service in one step, tires and swaps, readings, and billing.
sections.body_md:
Fleet keeps every car serviced: oil, tires, brakes, inspections and the registration. Finance bills what Fleet records. Recording a service resets its reminders and makes its bill.

## What is due

Open **Field work** > **Maintenance** (Finance: **Money** > **Maintenance bills**).

1. Every car, most urgent first: overdue (red), due soon, no record yet (dashed), all OK.
2. Your To do has one Service due task per car listing what is due. Open it: the car opens with the record pop-up.
3. A car with no record yet has one task to record its last service. Enter what you know once.

## Record a service

1. Press **Record a service** on the car (or **Record** on one item of the car's Maintenance).
2. Tick what was done, check the date and the odometer, type the shop, the cost before HST and the HST, and add the receipt.
3. Who pays: the owner for an owner's car (deducted on their statement), CarmaCars for a company car, a claim, the renter, or no charge.
4. Leave **The bill is in: bill it now** ticked, or untick it and press **Bill now** on the record later.
5. Press **Record the service**. The items done are OK again.

> Watch out: Above your single limit the service is recorded and the timers reset, but an Admin bills it: you see "An Admin bills it".

## Tires, swaps and readings

- Under Tires: **Add a tire set** (kind, size, brand, tread, made and bought dates, where it is stored), **Put on the car** to swap.
- Ontario: winter tires on by December 1 (reminder from November 1), off after April 1. Tires are due soon at 4 mm of tread, overdue at 3 mm.
- **Add a reading** when you see the odometer. Handover, return and move readings come in by themselves.
- A car whose recorded safety inspection or registration has expired cannot be handed over until the renewal is recorded.

sections.title: Shared tools
sections.blurb: The calendar and Find a renter.
sections.body_md:
Every function has the calendar and Find a renter. Use them to answer questions fast.

## Which cars are free (release 44)

At the top of **Calendar**: choose the **Pickup** and the **Return** the customer wants and you see every car at once.

1. Each car says **Available** (green edge) or **Not available** (red edge), available cars first. A car that is not available says why: Booked, On rent, Booked, payment due, Placeholder (held), Maintenance, Cleaning, Blocked, Out of service or Leaving the fleet, with the booking number and the dates. It also says the **Next free** start for the same length of rental.
2. An offer or a request out on a car does not hold it: it shows as a note, and the car stays Available until the booking is paid.
3. Narrow it with **Class**, **Seats at least** and **Price a day up to**, or tick **Available only**.
4. Customer service and Sales: press **Offer these dates** on an available car. Send an offer opens with the car and the dates filled in; add the customer and send.
5. No customer's name or number is shown here. The answer is the same check the booking makes, so a car shown Available can be booked for those dates.

## The calendar

1. Every car with its photo, its bookings, requests and blocks, in the colours of the legend above it: on rent, confirmed, request, offer or hold, maintenance, block. The red line is now. Tap a bar for its details; on a phone it opens on the agenda, by day.
2. Use the arrows, Today and the range to move around, or search by plate, booking or name.
3. Fleet and customer service can remove a cleaning block from its side panel (**Remove the block**) when a car is ready sooner.

![](/guides/img/va-cs-09-calendar-desktop-541a6da5.jpg "desktop; size: 1230 800; address: carmacars.ca/va/calendar; pins: 1 60.2 33.8, 2 28.5 17.5")

## Find a car

**Bookings**, the **Find a car** tab. A renter quotes the car code on the car's page (like CC-7F3A).

1. Type the car code, a plate, a VIN or the name. Each car shows its code, plate, status and its page on the site.
2. In Add a rental, type the car code or plate in the box above Car to choose it.

## Find a renter

1. Search by name, email, phone or booking number.
2. Opening a renter's private details asks for a reason (**Open with a reason**). It is kept in the access log.
3. The renter's record has **Add a note** and the **Activity** log: everything about the renter, newest first, with a chip per type (All by default), **Search the activity**, **Older** for the next 50, and **Email**, **Call** and **Text**. Fleet does not see payments in it.

![](/guides/img/va-cs-07-renters-desktop-99cfd0ef.jpg "desktop; size: 1230 240; address: carmacars.ca/va/renters; pins: 1 68.3 34.6")

## Email the renter

Customer service, Sales, Fleet and Finance can all write to the renter from a booking: press **Email the renter**, or open the **Messages & history** section.

The booking page, the car page and the listing review are the same pages an Admin opens. The car page has the Admin's tabs your function uses: **Overview**, **Rates & fees** and **Maintenance** (Fleet), **Listing** and **Documents**; an old link to a car's maintenance opens its Maintenance tab. You see the sections and buttons of your function: Finance has the money, the refunds and the deposit; Fleet the field jobs, the handovers and the car's rates; customer service the review and offer, changes and extensions; Sales the requests and offers.

1. Write a **Subject** and a **Message**, or pick a **Quick reply** to start from.
2. Press **Email the renter**. It goes from CarmaCars and the renter can answer in their account; the answer opens a task for customer service.
3. On a booking an insurer pays you can choose Blind Spot Car Rental (insurance) as the sender, and **Email the adjuster** writes to the adjuster on the booking.

The form is under the booking's Activity log (release 35), which lists the messages both ways, every email of the booking, the texts, chat, calls, notes and the rest, newest first, with a chip per type and a search. Each email counts against the daily email limit, shown under the form with today's number.

### Find a booking
**Bookings**: type at least 3 characters of the booking number (CC-1042, 1042), the renter's or a driver's name, an email, a phone number, a plate or a car code, then press Enter. **My bookings** lists yours, with your commission. Every search is logged, as Find a renter.

## Phone alerts

Get an alert on your phone or computer for new requests, replies to answer and urgent problems, even with the portal closed.

1. Open **Profile** (top of the menu). Under **Phone alerts**, press **Turn on alerts** and allow notifications. The first page of the portal also offers it once.
2. Under **What to alert me about**: new requests, booking changes and messages are on for staff; payments are off until you tick them.
3. **Send a test alert** checks the device. **Remove** takes an old phone off.

On an iPhone, add CarmaCars to the Home Screen first (Safari, **Share**, **Add to Home Screen**). Use your phone's own Focus or Do Not Disturb for quiet hours.

### Search

The **Search** button at the top of every page (or press **/** where the page has no search box of its own) finds pages and the records your role may open: bookings and requests by number, renter name, email, phone or plate, renters, owners and cars.

### A VIN from the car

VIN fields have **Scan the barcode** (the barcode in the driver's door frame or under the windshield) and **Photo of the VIN**. Check what was read against the car before saving.

## Alerts by email

Alerts that are not urgent come together in one email at most once an hour; urgent ones (a payment declined, documents to review for a pickup within 2 hours, the site down) still come on their own. Every alert is in the bell and on your phone at once. Choose on **Profile**, Notifications: alerts by email, **Change how often**: Hourly digest, Daily digest (07:00) or Off.

> Tip: To change the email you sign in with, open Profile, Sign-in and press **Change my email**: type the new address, and we send a confirmation link to it and tell the old address. Your email changes only when the link is opened, and every record of yours follows it.

sections.title: Quick reference
sections.body_md:
### Where things are

| Item | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| **To do** | Next up, your lanes with their timers, then every open task |
| **Today at a glance** | The second tab of To do: pickups, returns, what is due |
| **Working as** | Switch function (above the menu) |
| **Customer service** | Requests, Visitors (Live now, Chat, History), Messages; More customer service |
| **Finance** | Money (To handle, By day, All payments, Refunds, Deposits, Reconciliation), Owner money, Tolls and tickets, Turo trips; More finance |
| **Fleet** | Field jobs, Fleet map, Checks, Maintenance; More fleet |
| **Sales** | Requests and offers, Visitors, Marketplace, My sales; More sales |
| **Add a rental, New quote, Send an offer** | Buttons: Add a rental on Bookings, New quote and Send an offer on Requests |
| **My numbers** | Scorecard (your results by week) and My sales (commissions, quotes, offers, bookings) |

### Top tasks

1. *Take a task:* **To do**, **Take it**, then **Done**
2. *Send an offer:* **Requests**, the booking, then **Send the offer**
3. *Quote a caller:* **Requests**, the **New quote** button, then **Create the request**
4. *See your sales:* **Me**, the **My sales** tab, then **By week** or **By month**
5. *Claim a client you found:* **I sourced this client** when you add the rental or send the offer
6. *Review Forms C and D:* **Owner forms** > **Approve**
7. *Read a toll notice:* **Tolls and tickets** > **Read a notice**
8. *Issue a refund:* **Request the refund**, **Issue the refund**
9. *Schedule a field job:* **Field jobs** > **Schedule**
10. *Cover a plate:* **Cover the plate**, **Save the covered photo**

### If something goes wrong

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| **A link says it expired** | Links in our emails work for 24 hours, once. Press **Send me a new link** on that page. |
| **"Error 1102" on a page** | A short limit on our web host. Reload the page. You are still signed in. |
| **"That email and password do not match an account."** | Check the address, or use **Set a new password** on the sign-in page. |
| **A task is above your limit** | Press **Escalate** and say why. An Admin picks it up. |
| **Asked for a 6-digit code** | Open your authenticator app. Lost your phone? Tell an Admin. |
